situation: After a heavy storm in Garoua, Halima sees a small channel cut into the red soil beside the road. The water has carried sand and small stones and dropped them further down the slope.
In her compound, a big rock has cracks and is slowly crumbling into sand at its base. Halima wonders which slow forces can break solid rock and carry away the soil.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Halima does not know which forces break rocks and carry away the soil.
What did the running water do beside the road?
It cut a channel in the soil, carried sand and stones, and dropped them further down the slope.
How can we protect the soil beside roads and in our compounds?
We can plant grass and trees, build small stone lines and drains, and avoid leaving the soil bare.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the processes that wear down the surface of the Earth and shape its landforms.

qa.a: Denudation is the wearing away and lowering of the surface of the Earth by weathering, erosion and transportation. The word means "to make bare".

sum.title: I. Definition
defs: Denudation (or degradation) is the wearing away and lowering of the surface of the Earth by weathering, erosion and transportation.

qa.q: The rock in Halima's compound crumbles in its place. Which process is this?
qa.a: This is weathering: the breaking down of rocks in their place, without movement.

qa.q: The water picked up sand and stones beside the road. Which process is this?
qa.a: This is erosion: the wearing away and picking up of rock and soil by a moving agent.

qa.q: During the Harmattan, dust from the Sahara reaches Garoua. Which process is this?
qa.a: This is transportation: the carrying of material from one place to another by an agent, here the wind.

sum.title: II. Major Processes of Denudation
items: A. Weathering
Weathering is the breaking down of rocks in their place (in situ), with no movement. Example: a rock that cracks in the sun.
denudation.png
B. Erosion
Erosion is the wearing away and picking up of rock and soil by a moving agent. Example: running water cutting a gully.
C. Transportation

Transportation is the carrying of eroded material from one place to another. Example: the Harmattan carrying dust from the Sahara. When the agent loses energy, it drops the material: this is deposition.

qa.q: Which agent of denudation is the most important in Garoua during the rainy season?
qa.a: Running water is the most important: rain and rivers like the Benue cut gullies and valleys and carry mud and sand.

qa.q: Where is the wind a strong agent of denudation?
qa.a: The wind is strong in dry areas with little vegetation, such as the Sahara and the Far North of Cameroon.

qa.q: Where do waves act in Cameroon?
qa.a: Waves act along the coast, for example at Limbe and Kribi, where they erode cliffs and build beaches.

sum.title: III. Main Agents of Denudation
defs: An agent of denudation is a natural force that erodes and transports material.
items: The Agents
– Running water: rain, streams and rivers. It is the most important agent (the Benue in the rainy season).
– Wind: strong in dry areas with little vegetation (Sahara, Far North).
– Waves: along the coast (Limbe, Kribi).
– Ice (glaciers) acts in cold regions and high mountains.

evaluation: Denudation is the wearing away of the surface of the Earth by weathering, erosion and transportation.
What is the difference between weathering and erosion?
Weathering breaks rocks in their place; erosion wears them away and moves them with an agent.
remediation: The breaking down of rocks in their place is ______.
The picking up of material by an agent is ______.
The most important agent of denudation is running ______.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. weathering 2. erosion 3. transportation 4. water 5. dry 6. coast
end.homework: Compare an old wall and a new wall in your area. Write three differences you see, and suggest what damaged the old wall.
bilingual: La dénudation / l'érosion au sens large
teacherNote: Correction: the source notes say that Garoua is in the Sahel. Garoua (about 9° N, about 1,000 mm of rain) is in the Sudanian savanna. The Sahel is further north, near Lake Chad.
Some books include deposition in denudation; the syllabus asks for weathering, erosion and transportation. Deposition is mentioned as the end of transportation.
